news.headline: Nasdaq 100 Rallies as Oil Slides, Yields Retreat: Stock Market Today
news.summary: Wall Street snapped a two-day losing streak Thursday as oil retreated from its geopolitical spike and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped back below 5%. Chipmakers led the rebound, with Intel, AMD and Micron all posting outsized gains, while gold climbed 2.5% to $4,369 an ounce. The bounce came one day after the Federal Reserve delivered its first interest rate hike since 2023 and signaled at least one more this year.
news.content_text: U.S. stocks rebounded sharply Thursday, erasing two sessions of losses as crude oil retreated from its geopolitical spike and Treasury yields eased back below 5%, one day after the Federal Reserve delivered its first interest rate hike since 2023. The S&P 500 rose 1.1% to 7,635.21, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average lagged with a 0.7% advance, up 365 points to 51,827.04.  The Nasdaq 100 outperformed, jumping 1.8% to 29,450.56. West Texas Intermediate fell 1.6% to $100.81 a barrel Brent dropped 2.5% to $103.23, a one-week low Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and a unanimous FOMC lifted the fed funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4% on Wednesday and projected at least one further increase this year, citing inflation that remains too high at 3.4% and a labor market at effectively full employment. Treasury Yields Retreat, Volatility Cools The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.95%, down 8 basis points and back under the 5.04% level hit earlier this week, which had marked a 19-year high. The policy-sensitive 2-year yield slipped 6 basis points to 4.69%, while the 30-year eased 7 basis points to 5.30%. The CBOE Volatility Index slid 11.4% to 15.69, unwinding the fear premium built up around the Fed decision and the Middle East supply scare. Gold was the standout in commodities, jumping 2.5% to $4,368.71 an ounce as real yields retreated, with silver surging 4.1% to $65.86.  On the macro front, initial jobless claims fell 10,000 to 196,000, well below the 206,500 consensus and close to July’s 60-year low, while the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index slowed to 37.8 from 47.4 but comfortably beat the 32.1 estimate. news.summary: Bloom Energy shares are trading higher Thursday as lower oil prices and bond yields boosted data center infrastructure stocks.
news.content_text: Bloom Energy Corp . (NYSE: BE ) shares are trading higher Thursday along with other data center infrastructure companies as falling oil prices and bond yields help risk assets rebound. Here’s what you need to know . Bloom Energy shares are advancing steadily. Why is BE stock advancing? Stocks Rebound as Oil and Yields Retreat Wall Street clawed back sharply Thursday after two rough sessions in a row, helped along by crude prices backing off their recent geopolitical-driven spike and bond yields dropping under the 5% mark, all coming just a day after the Federal Reserve pushed through its first rate increase in roughly three years. WTI crude slipped 1.6% down to $100.81 per barrel, while Brent fell even further, dropping 2.5% to settle at $103.23, its lowest mark in a week. Wednesday’s decision saw Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and every voting member of the FOMC agree to bump the federal funds rate a quarter point higher, landing in a fresh 3.75%-4% range. Retreating crude prices matter for Bloom Energy less because of direct energy costs and more because they ease inflation worries, reducing pressure on the Fed and encouraging investors back into riskier growth names. Falling Treasury yields have a more direct effect: since Bloom remains a capital-intensive, still-scaling business, its valuation leans heavily on future profits, and lower yields make those future earnings worth more in today’s dollars. Lower yields also reduce the cost of financing Bloom’s ongoing expansion, whether through debt or equity, making today’s macro backdrop a tailwind. news.headline: QUICK SPARK: Generac Soars Nearly 20% on $8 Billion Amazon Data Center Deal
news.summary: Generac opened 27.8% higher on a long-term generator supply agreement with Amazon, then eased to 19%. Initial deliveries total $2.4 billion.
news.content_text: Generac Holdings Inc. (NYSE: GNRC ) jumped 19.1% to $208.48 by late Thursday morning, pulling back modestly from an opening spike of 27.8% that had the stock poised for its best session ever. The catalyst for the move is a long-term supply agreement to provide industrial backup generators for Amazon.com Inc.’s (NASDAQ: AMZN ) global data center infrastructure. Initial deliveries total $2.4 billion across 2027 and 2028, with purchases potentially reaching $8 billion over the life of the deal. The agreement reprices Generac from a hurricane-season consumer name into AI infrastructure. Backup power has become a binding constraint on data center buildouts, and Amazon just locked up years of capacity with one supplier. The stock entered Thursday already up 41% over 30 days. QUICK CONTEXT: Generac Lands Amazon Data-Center Power Deal Generac disclosed on Sept. 16 that it entered a long-term supply arrangement tied to Amazon data centers, marking a major expansion of its role in backup power for large computing facilities. Under the filing, Generac issued Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings, an Amazon subsidiary, a warrant to buy up to 1.69 million Generac shares at $200.9266 each. About 307,954 shares vested immediately, while the rest vest as Amazon-related payments for data-center backup generators rise, up to $8 billion. The first deliveries under the arrangement are expected to total $2.4 billion in 2027 and 2028. Generac said the warrant can be exercised through Sept. 16, 2033, and is subject to standard adjustment provisions. Generac is a Wisconsin-based energy technology company founded in 1959. news.headline: 10-Year Yield Tops 5%, Oil Storms Past $105: Stock Market Today
news.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield broke 5% for the first time since 2007 as WTI surged past $105 on Saudi pipeline outages, pressuring stocks ahead of the Fed.
news.content_text: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield broke above 5% on Tuesday, and crude oil stormed past $105 a barrel, a combination that left every major U.S. equity index in the red at midday. President Donald Trump said on Truth Social that “the world’s diesel price rise is mostly caused by the Russia/Ukraine War, not Iran.” West Texas Intermediate crude jumped 3.7% to $105.12 a barrel after Saudi Aramco canceled or delayed cargoes to European refiners.  Brent crude rose 2.4% to $108.20. Heating oil surged 5.5% and gasoline futures climbed 3.2%, with U.S. diesel prices now averaging $6.26 a gallon, surpassing the previous record set in 2022. The 10-year Treasury yield rose for the fifth straight session, climbing to 5.04% before settling near 5.00%. The 30-year yield stood at 5.37% and the 20-year at 5.40%. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told lawmakers that “the need to address [the] deficit is one factor affecting 10-year treasury bond yield,” while stressing the Treasury does “not set equilibrium price for yield levels.” Traders are assigning roughly a 92% probability to a 25-basis-point rate hike from the Federal Reserve on Wednesday, which would be the first increase since July 2023.  Across U.S. equity markets by midday Tuesday, losses were broad-based but orderly, with nine of 11 S&P 500 sectors lower. The S&P 500 slipped 0.5% to 7,580.85, hitting its lowest level in three weeks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was the clear laggard, shedding 496 points, or 1%, to 51,925.70.  The Nasdaq 100 fell 0.6% to 28,946.97. news.summary: Twist Bioscience joins Eli Lilly's TuneLab platform, supplying high-throughput antibody data to train advanced AI drug prediction models.
news.content_text: Twist Bioscience Corporation (NASDAQ: TWST ) on Wednesday announced an agreement with Lilly TuneLab, a collaborative AI/ML drug discovery platform created by Eli Lilly and Co. (NYSE: LLY ) . Twist is a provider of antibody characterization data services for TuneLab, including for AbLab, an antibody developability prediction model. Read Also: Twist Bioscience Stock Resilient Despite Scorpion Capital Short Report Integrating High-Quality Wet Lab Data With AI Drug Discovery TuneLab was created to accelerate biotech innovation by enabling participating companies to access AI/ML drug discovery models trained on decades of Lilly’s proprietary research data. Participating companies may use the TuneLab prediction models to more rapidly down-select candidate molecules. Through this agreement, users will be able to order antibody services from Twist using TuneLab preferred Twist protocols to generate high-quality wet lab data. Leadership Commentary On AI Data Scaling And Federated Training “Twist has the scale and high-throughput capabilities to generate consistent and reliable antibody characterization data these models need to be trained on. Lilly’s leadership in empowering AI-enabled drug discovery and its impressive network of partnerships create a powerful ecosystem that brings together advanced models and high-quality data,” said Emily Leproust , CEO and co-founder of Twist Bioscience. In August, Anthropic selected Twist Bioscience as an independent evaluator for a protein design campaign using its Claude Opus 4.8 and Mythos Preview artificial intelligence models . news.content_text: U.S. stocks rebounded sharply Thursday, erasing two sessions of losses as crude oil retreated from its geopolitical spike and Treasury yields eased back below 5%, one day after the Federal Reserve delivered its first interest rate hike since 2023. The S&P 500 rose 1.1% to 7,635.21, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average lagged with a 0.7% advance, up 365 points to 51,827.04.  The Nasdaq 100 outperformed, jumping 1.8% to 29,450.56. West Texas Intermediate fell 1.6% to $100.81 a barrel Brent dropped 2.5% to $103.23, a one-week low Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and a unanimous FOMC lifted the fed funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4% on Wednesday and projected at least one further increase this year, citing inflation that remains too high at 3.4% and a labor market at effectively full employment. Treasury Yields Retreat, Volatility Cools The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.95%, down 8 basis points and back under the 5.04% level hit earlier this week, which had marked a 19-year high. The policy-sensitive 2-year yield slipped 6 basis points to 4.69%, while the 30-year eased 7 basis points to 5.30%. The CBOE Volatility Index slid 11.4% to 15.69, unwinding the fear premium built up around the Fed decision and the Middle East supply scare. Gold was the standout in commodities, jumping 2.5% to $4,368.71 an ounce as real yields retreated, with silver surging 4.1% to $65.86.  On the macro front, initial jobless claims fell 10,000 to 196,000, well below the 206,500 consensus and close to July’s 60-year low, while the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index slowed to 37.8 from 47.4 but comfortably beat the 32.1 estimate. news.headline: Elon Musk's Starlink Not a Threat to Wireless Carriers, Says T-Mobile CFO: ‘You Can Have a Million Satellites…’
news.summary: T-Mobile CFO Pete Osvaldik says Starlink can't replace wireless networks due to signal limits, though it may aid rural broadband.
news.content_text: T-Mobile US Inc. ‘s (NASDAQ: TMUS ) Chief Financial Officer Pete Osvaldik says that Space Exploration Technologies Corp. ‘s (NASDAQ: SPCX ) Starlink is not a threat to traditional telecom operators. The Fundamental Laws of Physics Osvaldik, speaking at Citigroup Inc. ‘s (NYSE: C ) 2026 Global TMT Conference on Wednesday, pushed back on the idea that satellite-to-phone service can replace traditional wireless networks. The company argued that distance-related signal limits make the technology unsuitable as a full alternative, especially indoors. Osvaldik also said that SpaceX would need “probably over a billion femtocells to have the equivalent outdoor coverage with all the interference problems.” A Femtocell is a device that improves indoor cellular coverage and data speeds. “It’s not a competitive threat” from a wireless perspective, Osvaldik said, but acknowledged that it could pose challenges in the broadband sector, as they can solve challenges with “spectral assets” and “external powered antennas,” Osvaldik said, adding that SpaceX could see success in the rural and suburban regions.
